## Problem

Discovered-from CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9 (Add a Favicon).

The favicon epic wired the icon into the **core repo's** `index.html` and `public/404.html`, but each game repository (`tce-<game>`) is its own Vite app with its **own** `index.html` entry point and its own `public/` dir (the core never owns game HTML). When a game is run standalone (`npm run dev` in `tce-<game>`), the browser tab shows no icon and requests `/favicon.ico` → 404.

Observed live: the `tce-main-street` dev server on `:3000` serves `tce-main-street/index.html`, which declares no icon/manifest links, and its `./core` submodule was pinned pre-icon-commits.

## Affected repos

The following sibling game repos each have their own `index.html` with zero `rel="icon"` links (verified 2026-10-05):

- tce-beleaguered-castle, tce-blackjack, tce-coloretto, tce-feudalism, tce-golf, tce-lost-cities, tce-main-street, tce-sushi-go

## Desired change

For each game repo:

1. Bump the `./core` submodule to a commit that includes the icon work (CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9).
2. Add base-relative icon links to the game's `index.html` (favicon SVG, Apple touch icon, web manifest) and to its `404.html` if present — same convention as the core:
   ```html
   <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="favicon.svg" />
   <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="apple-touch-icon.png" />
   <link rel="manifest" href="site.webmanifest" />
   ```
3. Make the icon assets available to the game's Vite dev/build. Options: (a) compose the core's `public/` icon files into the game's `public/` via the existing game-asset composition path, or (b) a small shared Vite plugin that serves/copies the core's icon set. Decide during plan; keep a single source of truth (the core's `public/favicon.svg`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every affected `tce-<game>` repo's `index.html` declares the favicon (and ideally Apple touch + manifest) with base-relative hrefs, and the referenced files resolve in both dev (`npm run dev`) and production builds.
2. `/favicon.ico` either resolves or is no longer requested (see companion item on the .ico fallback).
3. A test per repo (or a shared core test that scans sibling repos) asserts the game entry declares the icon links.
4. Full test suite of each touched repo passes; changes pushed to that repo's `dev` only.

## Notes

Out of scope of the original epic per its intake ("no per-game favicons"); recorded as discovered work rather than absorbed. Cross-repo: push each game repo to its own `dev` branch, never `main`.
data.title: Wire the app icon into each tce-<game> repo entry (index.html + public/ icons)

data.description:
## Problem

Discovered-from CG-0MUTTXRWZ009NUB9 (Add a Favicon).

The app declares an SVG favicon (`<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="favicon.svg" />`), which modern browsers honour. However browsers and tooling still request `/favicon.ico` unconditionally as a fallback (observed: `GET /favicon.ico 404` on the dev server). On a cold load with no declared icon, or in tools that only look for `.ico`, this produces a 404 and a generic tab icon.

## Desired change

Generate and serve a real `/favicon.ico` from the tracked tableau emblem (`public/favicon.svg`) alongside the existing PNG variants, so the fallback request resolves.

- Extend `scripts/generate-app-icons.ts` with an `.ico` target (multi-resolution 16/32/48 px, produced with `sharp`'s `toFormat('ico')` if available, or an ICO container built from the PNG buffers) written to `public/favicon.ico`.
- Keep the SVG as the primary `rel="icon"`; add a defensive `<link rel="icon" href="favicon.ico" sizes="any" />` after it.
- Extend `tests/scripts/generate-app-icons.test.ts` to assert the `.ico` artefact exists, has the ICO signature, and contains at least one image; extend the build-output test to assert `favicon.ico` is present in `dist/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run generate:icons` produces `public/favicon.ico` from the emblem, and the file is committed.
2. `index.html` references `favicon.ico` as a fallback icon link.
3. Tests assert the `.ico` is generated (signature + non-empty) and present in the production build output.
4. Full suite passes.

## Notes

Low priority — the SVG favicon works in modern browsers; this is robustness for legacy/tooling fallback requests. Out of scope of the original epic's ACs (which only required a favicon link), recorded as discovered work.
data.title: Serve a real /favicon.ico fallback so browsers/tools stop 404ing

## Follow-up from a live 404 report

An operator reported `GET /favicon.ico 404` and `favicon.ico:1 GET ... 404 (Not Found)` while a dev server was running. Investigation:

- The server on `:3000` was the **Main Street** game dev server (`/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`), not the core repo. It serves `tce-main-street/index.html` (no icon links) and its `./core` submodule predates the icon commits.
- The **core** repo's work is correct: a fresh core dev server serves `favicon.svg` as `image/svg+xml`, `site.webmanifest` as `application/manifest+json`, and all PNGs as `image/png` (verified on :3099).
- Two gaps fall outside this epic's ACs (the intake explicitly scoped out per-game favicons):
  1. **CG-0MUUFZSE90061KKL** — each `tce-<game>` repo has its own `index.html`/entry and needs the icon wiring + a `./core` submodule bump (8 repos affected).
  2. **CG-0MUUG00VV007ECXM** — browsers/tools still request `/favicon.ico`; add a generated `.ico` fallback for robustness.

Both are recorded as `discovered-from` this item (no dependency edge that blocks it) and are **not** part of the delivered scope.
